maria: Heads-up - after the rw-model-v5 bump to staging we're seeing p95/p99 climb on short-chat traffic (~8-12 tokens). p95 went from 42ms -> 78ms.
raj: Saw that too. Initial flame graph points to a different kernel being picked for 8-token batches. kernel_selector now picks conv_v2 instead of conv_v1 for seq<=16.
linh: Also seeing KV cache miss rate spike in the same window. cache hit went from 87% -> 42% for those requests.
ci-bot: perf-check: staging/p95 +85%, p99 +120% for job rw-model-v5-onboard. See /artifacts/perf/3512345678.
maria: My hypothesis: tokenizer normalization change in PR 0f7c9a1 toggled strip_leading_space -> false which changed tokenization boundaries for many prompts. That shifted the KV prefixes (we key by model+token-prefix-hash) so prefix caching warmed down.
raj: ugh, that would cause a cache key divergence. Was that PR intended for model compatibility?
linh: It was to fix a multilingual spacing bug, but it wasn't pinned behind a skip-caching flag. The KV key uses tokenizer.encode(text) directly.
maria: Quick repro on my laptop: 
```
# before revert (v5 on staging)
> echo \"Hello there\" | python -c \"from tokenizer import encode; print(encode('Hello there'))\"
[1543, 28, 900]
# after local revert to pre-0f7c9a1
[43, 1543, 28, 900]
```
linh: That explains the miss. Our prefix cache only stores up to 4-token prefixes; shifting insertions changes alignment.
raj: Profiling snapshot from the slow request (staging):
```
Hot kernels (seq 8):
  conv_v2_forward  48.1%  (was 19.7% baseline)
  matmul_qk 23.4%  (slightly up)
  kv_cache_lookup 12.6% (was 3.2%)
```
maria: Note kv_cache_lookup increasing indicates more cache population work and evictions. Also batcher is forming different bucket sizes because token lengths changed -> more small batches = bad kernel for throughput.
sre-oncall: Can we pause the rollout? Current canary group is 5% traffic. Ops ready to throttle.
maria: Yes please pause. I'm opening a canary-pause via console now and reverting the tokenizer commit in staging.
raj: Proposed immediate actions:
- pause canary (maria)
- revert 0f7c9a1 on staging (raj)
- add a short-term shim: normalize tokens to previous behavior for KV key computation until we fix tokenizer compatibility (linh)
- add a perf presubmit that asserts no >10% regression on p95 for common short-chat traces
linh: I'll add the shim: Tokenizer.encode_for_kv(text) -> previous_normalize(text) before encoding. Patch ready in branch kv-shim-3512.
ci-bot: presubmit perf job queued: perf/presubmit/kv-shim-3512.
maria: After revert, staging p95 dropped back to 44ms, p99 stable. kv hit rate back to 85% within ~10 minutes of warmup.
raj: Long-term: we should decouple KV key from raw tokenizer outputs (use canonicalized prefix or fingerprinting that tolerates normalization changes) and add a migration path for tokenizer changes.
linh: Agreed. I'll write a short RFC and a migration plan. Also will add a unit test that ensures tokenizer changes preserve prefix distributions for top 100k sample prompts.
sre-oncall: Thanks for the quick mitigation. Leaving the canary paused until the revert is fully rolled out and perf baseline validated.
maria: Filing follow-up: ACTION-351234 - add perf presubmit, implement KV shim, RFC for tokenizer->kv contract.
raj: Thanks team :thumbsup:
ci-bot: note: created artifact /artifacts/perf/3512345678/compare.html showing before/after revert metrics.
__notes: Generated synthetic Slack thread about model onboarding perf regression tied to tokenizer normalization causing KV cache key divergence and kernel selection changes. Messages are short and reflect realistic engineering coordination. All timestamps are strings to match agents.md constraints.
